rows.note: This is the all-purpose choice or preference equivalent, especially in “would rather” statements.

example.english: I’d rather stay home than go out.
example.traditional: 我寧願留喺屋企，都唔想出去。
example.jyutping: ngo5 ning4 jyun6 lau4 hai2 uk1 kei2 dou1 m4 soeng2 ceot1 heoi3

rows.note: Use this before an adjective when “rather” means fairly or quite, as in “rather good.”

example.english: The food at this restaurant is rather good.
example.traditional: 呢間餐廳啲嘢食幾好喎。
example.jyutping: ni1 gaan1 caan1 teng1 di1 je5 sik6 gei2 hou2 wo3

rows.note: Use this when “rather” introduces a result or statement contrary to what was expected.

example.english: It rained, but I rather enjoyed it.
example.traditional: 估唔到落雨，我反而幾享受。
example.jyutping: gu2 m4 dou2 lok6 jyu5 ngo5 faan2 ji4 gei2 hoeng2 sau6

rows.note: Use this to correct or refine what you have just said, meaning “or rather, more precisely.”

example.english: It’s not that I don’t like it—or rather, I’m just not used to it.
example.traditional: 我唔係唔鍾意，或者應該話，我只係未習慣。
example.jyutping: ngo5 m4 hai6 m4 zung1 ji3 waak6 ze2 jing1 goi1 waa6 ngo5 zi2 hai6 mei6 zaap6 gwaan3
